Living Well / Resource directory

Learn something and keep room for reflection

Start with life

What would be useful?

Explore a real question, preserve sources, and decide what belongs in your own life.

The simpler starting point: Choose one question and one resource in a format you enjoy. A conversation or a few pages can be enough.

Finish when: You can describe what you encountered, what remains uncertain, and whether another step would help.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

How AI Works

Consider it when: You want a manageable introduction to AI concepts.

Check first: Keep an explanation of a technology separate from claims about its value in your circumstances.

Access: Free public videos and lesson material; no account needed for the introductory video page.

Watch the introductory video · Full context and source

A first encounter with philosophy

Consider it when: You want an introductory philosophical question to work through.

Check first: Begin with a section rather than treating course completion as a requirement.

Access: Free course text can be started without registration; progress, quizzes, and participation features use an account.

Start Introducing philosophy · Full context and source

ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography

Consider it when: You want to retain a few sources behind an idea.

Check first: Check their actual arguments instead of relying on citation formatting.

Access: Free browser service without an account or installation. It uses browser storage; sharing a saved version uploads that version.

Open ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography · Full context and source

On Being: a conversation about attention

Consider it when: A thoughtful conversation is a better entry than a lesson.

Check first: Listen to the speaker’s perspective without making it a universal prescription.

Access: Free web audio and transcript; no subscription needed for this selection.

Mary Oliver in conversation · Full context and source

Religious traditions, with context

Consider it when: You want context before comparing spiritual traditions.

Check first: Keep traditions and interpretations distinct.

Access: Free public essays; no registration needed to read.

Rivers of Faith · Full context and source

A brief guided pause

Consider it when: You are curious about a short optional attention practice.

Check first: Choose a suitable format, adapt or stop when unhelpful, and do not treat it as professional care.

Access: Free web audio; transcripts for some recordings. An app is optional.

UCLA guided recordings and transcripts · Full context and source

Poetry Unbound: one poem at a time

Consider it when: You want to encounter a poem without extracting a productivity lesson.

Check first: Follow the original and leave room for a response that is not an action plan.

Access: Free episode audio and transcript; books and other offerings are separate.

Ada Limón: Wonder Woman · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Use technology for a bounded contribution

A search, reading aid, or generated question can support inquiry. Keep factual verification and your own interpretation separate from the confidence of a response.

Do not upload a private life to find a question

An AI system can offer generic reflection questions without receiving your journal. Answer away from the service when privacy matters.

Allow an open ending

A spiritual or philosophical question does not need a manufactured resolution. Reading for interest, pleasure, or greater understanding is already a legitimate outcome.

Published as a selection path, not a personal field note. Source dates and access limits belong to each resource. No paid placement or affiliation is implied.
